population.note: FICTIONAL. Current users are ≈64.6M of ~267M adults. By age: 18–29 13.5% of 53M = 7.2M; 30–49 28% of 88M = 24.6M; 50–64 37% of 63M = 23.3M; 65+ 15% of 63M = 9.5M; total 64.6M = 24.2%. The income thirds average to the national figure: (32+25+15.5)/3 = 24.2. Cycling arithmetic: ever 33.6% − current 24.2% = 9.4% of adults have used and are off now. Of the 16.5 pts who had used by 2028, 11.2 are on now (about 6.4 who stayed on plus 4.8 off-now people who restarted, mostly on pills) and 5.3 are off. Of the 17.1 pts of new starters in this window, 13.0 are on and 4.1 are off. Cyclers among current users: 4.8 returners + ≈3.2 of the 2028 second-course users still on + ≈1.0 new starters already on a second course = 9.0. Add ≈2.0 off-now people who restarted and stopped again: (9.0+2.0)/33.6 = 33% cycled. That is down from 40% because a flood of first-timers enlarges the ever-used base. Persistence is higher than in 2028 for three reasons. One-year persistence on cash-pay daily pills is ~50%, against ~35% for injectables in 2026–28. Most starts came after the August 2029 oral-parity launch, so most new users are under 12 months in. Cash payers self-select. Off-drug population: ~25M adults have used and stopped, and ~177M have never used. The never-users are concentrated in the bottom third: the uninsured, Medicaid enrollees in states without coverage who don't smoke, people whose employer coverage ended and who won't pay $149–249 a month, and a small but vocal group of deliberate refusers. Pediatric: ~0.6% of under-18s (≈440k), mostly adolescents 12+ on semaglutide. The amycretin pill is not labelled under 18, but upper-income families obtain it off-label. A growing group of teenagers has a parent on the drug and a family table that grazes.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed Jan 2030 through Dec 2032 at a renegotiated ~$199/month with the $50 copay unchanged. Criteria are unchanged, and the documented body-composition counselling visit is still required. ≈3.6M beneficiaries use it for obesity: 3.6M × $199 × 12 ≈ $8.6B/yr federal spend. Medicare overall (Bridge plus Part D diabetes and cardiovascular codes) pays 15% of fills ≈ 9.7M users, consistent with 9.5M adults 65+ (15%) plus ~0.2–0.3M disabled under-65 enrollees. Medicaid pays 8% ≈ 5.2M users, at ~$199 under the supplemental rebate. Most of the growth from 2.6M comes through the smoking-cessation indication (Mar 2029). Existing federal law requires Medicaid to cover FDA-approved tobacco-cessation drugs, so states must cover semaglutide for cessation in 12-week courses, usually two courses a year. Weight-indication coverage is still state by state. The Indiana and Arkansas adherence waivers remain in force.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 80+ generic semaglutide brands, $6–40/month, plus generic oral semaglutide. Canada, Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and China sell generic semaglutide; generic liraglutide is everywhere. Tirzepatide and amycretin are still branded worldwide. US exclusivity runs to ~2031–32.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. In Jan 2030 TrumpRx and direct channels cut injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide to ~$199–275. Oral starting doses stay at $149. Maintenance pills (Foundayo high dose, Wegovy pill 25 mg) are $199. Oral amycretin is $149 to start and $249 at maintenance. Retatrutide is $299 on TrumpRx with its list cut to $1,299; supply is still allocated but loosening. Wegovy list remains $1,349. Payer mix of ~64.6M users: commercial 22% (14.2M, mostly diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnea, CKD and tobacco codes), Medicare 15% (9.7M), Medicaid 8% (5.2M), cash/direct 47% (30.4M), gray/imported 8% (5.2M) = 100%. Cash outlay is ≈30.4M × ~$180 average × 12 ≈ $66B/yr out of pocket. Employers that dropped weight coverage often offer an employee-paid 'voluntary benefit' direct contract at $179–229. That is cash under another name: no PBM gating, but also no subsidy. The two tiers are clear. Coded patients pay copays. Everyone else pays roughly a phone bill if they can afford it, or buys Indian pens and pills by mail. FDA still seizes parcels selectively and has not prosecuted individuals.

GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral parity is realised by Novo's oral amycretin, the NDA filed Jun 2028 in the parent world. FDA approved it Aug 2029, 14 months after filing. The label shows ~22% mean loss at 72 weeks, statistically matching tirzepatide in a head-to-head, though still below retatrutide's 28%. GI discontinuation is higher than with tirzepatide, and titration is slow. Survodutide was approved Feb 2029 and sells mostly into MASH. MariTide (monthly) filed with FDA in May 2029; the review was extended over GI tolerability data, and a decision is expected Q1 2031, so it is not on the market. Bimagrumab and other muscle-preserving adjuncts entered phase 3 in 2029 and are not on the US market. Semaglutide gained smoking cessation (Mar 2029) and gambling disorder (Sep 2030, priority review, built on a phase 3 that an NIH–academic consortium started in 2027). Lilly has an orforglipron trial in alcohol use disorder in phase 3. The incretin market is ≈$170B in 2030: US volume more than doubled, net prices fell ~15–25%, and generics keep eroding ex-US revenue.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Oral amycretin titration has the highest GI discontinuation of the oral agents (~10%).
Elevated with rapid loss. The absolute number of cases rises with the user base.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; litigation continues, with an MDL bellwether trial scheduled for 2031.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The population problem persists. The 65+ user count has roughly doubled, so absolute cases rise even where counselling is followed. Cash-pay pill users mostly skip DEXA.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling and the Medicare Bridge counselling visit retained. There is no requirement for cash or telehealth channels.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Hazard ratios of ~1.3–1.4 in 65+ long-term users are replicated in a second cohort. The cycling effect is confirmed as additive in women. Short-half-life pills used with weekend holidays have not been studied for bone.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling and DEXA recommendation retained. Senate HELP report (2029) faulted Novo's disclosure. A DOJ civil settlement is pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; FDA warnings-section mention unchanged.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association in updated EMA, MHRA and FDA Sentinel analyses. This is now distinguished explicitly from anhedonia.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed Jan 2026 and has not returned.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Retatrutide postmarketing studies used SHAPS (Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale) and found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~9% at top doses against ~3% on placebo. A pooled reanalysis of trials that used SHAPS gives ~6% against ~3% across maintenance doses, dose-dependent, and largely reversible within 4–8 weeks of stopping. Real-world self-report surveys are higher, at 10–18%. Applied to ~64.6M users, the label's excess rate implies roughly 2M people with a drug-attributable clinically meaningful anhedonia at any time.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label update (Dec 2029) adds anhedonia/emotional blunting to Warnings and Precautions with the trial prevalence figures. The Medication Guide advises dose reduction and mood check-ins. There is no boxed warning. The gambling and smoking labels cite the same mechanism as the therapeutic rationale.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Substantial regain within a year of stopping. Involuntary stops now come mostly from employer coverage withdrawals and the end of 12-week cessation courses, not only from adherence gates.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly. Indiana waiver litigation is on appeal in the 7th Circuit.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signals for iron, B12, vitamin D and protein persist, especially in high-loss and low-income imported-product users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional society guidance updated 2029; nothing formal from FDA.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~7 years of continuous use; adolescents on drugs for decades; repeated cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exist. Adolescent bone-accrual studies are enrolling, with no readout.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements; pediatric bone-accrual studies ongoing.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imported volume has roughly quadrupled to ~5.2M users. Poison-centre calls about mail-order pens and pills keep rising; counterfeit 'amycretin' pills appeared in 2030.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Import alerts, selective parcel seizures, no individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.effect: Drug-holiday rebound (appetite surges, binge episodes and GI re-titration on resuming)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New in this window. Short-half-life pills (orforglipron, oral amycretin) make weekend and event holidays easy. Clinicians and ER reports describe vomiting on restart at full dose and binge eating during holidays. No controlled data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. FDA added a Medication Guide line in 2030 saying not to restart at full dose after missing more than 3 days.

food_and_beverage.state: The second volume wave arrived with the pills. US household volumes in salty snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks fell an estimated 4–7% across the two years, now including middle-income and suburban households. Majors cut SKUs, shrank packs and pushed 'portion-honest' lines. Protein, fibre, calcium and 'GLP-1 friendly' claims are table stakes. A small opposite niche is growing on the backlash: heritage, 'whole appetite' and full-fat brands marketed as unmedicated eating.

alcohol.state: Contraction broadened. Medicaid cessation courses are reaching smokers who also drink, and the anhedonia label made 'I just don't want it' a recognised condition. Beer and mainstream spirits volumes keep falling. Premium single-serve and NA lines hold. Tobacco volumes fall faster than trend in the bottom income third, and vape makers report GLP-1-linked declines.

restaurants.state: Traffic softens modestly and check sizes fall. Chains add half-portions and protein plates as standard. Buffets and all-you-can-eat formats close stores in high-uptake metros. Destination dining sells 'off-dose weekend' tasting menus. The flagged risk is not collapse but a slow drift to lower spend per visit.

apparel.state: Size churn is now permanent. Plus-size specialists stabilise, helped by people regaining after coverage loss and by backlash-aligned brands. Mainstream retailers carry wider runs and rental/resale 'between sizes' programmes.

fitness.state: Still growing: strength training, DEXA-plus-coaching chains and Medicare Advantage strength benefits. Cash pill users rarely buy the coaching, so growth is concentrated in the top third.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management falls from 58% to 43%. Large employers cite the volume surge after oral parity and flat pharmacy budgets. Coverage concentrates on diabetes, cardiovascular, sleep-apnea, CKD and tobacco codes, and PBMs audit those diagnoses for upcoding. Voluntary-benefit direct contracts replace coverage, so the employee pays. Where coverage is kept, adherence gating persists.

pharma.state: Volume roughly doubles. Novo partly recovers on oral amycretin despite the bone scandal. Lilly leads injectables with retatrutide and tirzepatide and orals with Foundayo. US net prices drift down through TrumpRx and Bridge renegotiation. Sector deal themes are muscle-preservation adjuncts and compulsion indications.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Being on the drug is now ordinary across the insured and the cash-paying middle class, and it no longer signals status. Being visibly unmedicated is the new signal, read either as poverty, as coverage loss, or as a statement. The 'on it too long' stoop in older users is still noticed. A new tell is the person who is lively on Saturday and quiet on Tuesday.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rises in every third (32/25/15.5%), but the gap widens in points. The top third pairs pills with DEXA and coaching. The middle third pays cash for pills with no monitoring. The bottom third gets in through tobacco codes in 12-week Medicaid courses or Indian imports, and cycles with them. In Dallas–Fort Worth's finance and insurance workforce, use among women 45–60 is past half. Lunch spots there sell 'off-day' plates for Fridays.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are smaller, and 'off-dose' feasts are scheduled: weddings, Thanksgiving and anniversaries are planned around pill holidays. Backlash congregations and fat-liberation groups host deliberately abundant potlucks as a counter-ritual. The two practices sit in the same towns.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'On', 'off' and now 'holidays weekends' appear on dating profiles. The anhedonia label gave partners a word to use. 'Are you blunted or just tired?' is a recognisable line. Some couples sync holidays; some backlash-aligned apps market 'unmedicated' matching.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is still medicalised, but the backlash has made it contested again. One camp treats craving as pathology to dose down. The other treats it as God-given, as a natural signal, or as the self. The gambling indication sharpened the argument by extending 'appetite' to money and screens.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. Labelled since Dec 2029 at ~6% clinically meaningful anhedonia against ~3% on placebo across maintenance doses, ~9% at top doses (SHAPS-based). Real-world self-report is 10–18%. With ~64.6M users, an excess of ~3 pts means roughly 2M people with label-grade drug-attributable blunting, and several million more who say they feel 'flat'. Dose reduction and drug holidays are common practice. In surveys, about a third of pill users report skipping deliberately at least once a month.
interior_life.framing: A side effect with a name and a number, which made it discussable rather than marginal. It is simultaneously the therapeutic mechanism in the smoking and gambling labels. Clinicians say 'dose-dependent anhedonia'. Users say 'flat', 'blunted', 'on-dose'. Backlash groups call it 'the grey'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: With coverage retreating, HR dashboards see less. Cash pill users are invisible to employers, and adherence gating affects a shrinking share. DOT sleep-apnea screening still ties some drivers to tirzepatide. Short-half-life pills mean workers take holidays on Fridays and weekends and resume Sunday night. Managers in sales and hospitality notice the Monday–Tuesday dip and joke about it. A few employers' EAPs now offer 'dose coaching'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Albums and comedy specials are marketed as 'made off-dose'. Touring musicians and chefs plan holidays openly. Fan forums argue over whether a songwriter's new record is 'blunted'. Weekend nightlife has a visible Friday-night surge from people on holiday, followed by GI-heavy Sundays.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists now cite the label at intake. Couples schedule holidays for anniversaries and conception attempts. Reduced desire is a common reason given for lowering dose, and partners of users join online support groups.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The anhedonia label armed the backlash coalition. Fat-acceptance activists, MAHA-adjacent 'natural' wellness and some evangelical congregations share platforms against 'medicating the appetite God gave us', though they disagree on almost everything else. The India price gap and employer retreat stay stump issues. Pundits speculate about a 'blunted electorate', but there is no turnout or polling evidence for it.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and fast on approvals (survodutide, oral amycretin, cessation and gambling indications), and now willing to label psychiatric effects with numbers. The anhedonia label came without a boxed warning or REMS. Enforcement against compounders is complete, and enforcement against imports stays selective even as the import volume quadruples.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. The Medicare Bridge was renewed at $199/$50. TrumpRx prices stepped down in Jan 2030. Medicaid cessation coverage flows from existing federal law, not new action. No new state legislation or waivers in this window.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The Indiana and Arkansas waivers remain in force (≥80% proportion-of-days-covered plus quarterly verified weigh-ins), and the 7th Circuit appeal is pending. PBM adherence gating persists in the shrinking pool of employers that still cover weight management. BMI-linked wellness surcharges of up to 30% of premium remain allowed. The cash channel has no conditioning or monitoring at all, so the surveillance tier and the unmonitored tier now sit side by side.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still steers commercial drivers onto tirzepatide. Army accession policy is unchanged and contested. No new mandates.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Indian mail-order generics, now ~5.2M US users, remain an irritant in trade talks. Section 232 tariffs are still cited to justify the price floor. Novo has expanded US fill-finish capacity for amycretin to blunt the tariff argument.

events.event: FDA approves semaglutide as an adjunct for smoking cessation; under existing federal tobacco-cessation coverage rules, state Medicaid programmes and ACA-compliant plans must cover it in 12-week courses, and enrollment in quitline-linked prescriptions surges in the bottom income third

FDA approves Novo Nordisk's oral amycretin, a daily pill matching tirzepatide's ~22% weight loss in a head-to-head trial; TrumpRx lists it at $149 to start and $249 at maintenance, and telehealth starts double within two quarters

Annual employer benefits survey finds the share of large employers covering GLP-1s for weight management has fallen to 43%; several Fortune 100 firms replace coverage with employee-paid direct-to-manufacturer 'voluntary benefit' contracts and restrict plan coverage to diabetes, cardiac and sleep-apnea codes

FDA adds anhedonia/emotional blunting to Warnings and Precautions across the incretin class, citing ~6% versus ~3% placebo on the SHAPS scale, rising to ~9% at top doses, and advises dose reduction for affected patients
CMS renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2032 at ~$199 a month with the $50 copay unchanged; Lilly and Novo cut TrumpRx injectable prices to ~$199–275, keeping oral starting doses at $149

FDA grants semaglutide a priority-review approval as an adjunct to CBT for adult gambling disorder, the first compulsion indication, two weeks after an 'Unblunted' rally in Nashville joins fat-liberation groups, natural-health influencers and Southern Baptist pastors against 'medicating appetite'

open_tensions: The same reward-dampening mechanism now carries a Warnings label, at ~6% clinically meaningful anhedonia, and is the approved rationale for the smoking and gambling indications. Prescribers, payers and the backlash each cite the same label for opposite conclusions.

Access has split into a coded, copay tier and an unmonitored cash and import tier of ~35M people. Bone, muscle and anhedonia monitoring reach mainly the coded tier, while the cash tier holds most of the new users.
Twelve-week Medicaid cessation courses and employer withdrawals produce built-in on/off cycling in the bottom third, just as the fracture data say cycling compounds bone loss in women.
Short-half-life pills make drug holidays easy and common, but no one has studied the bone, rebound or cardiovascular effects of weekly on/off exposure across tens of millions of people.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide exists in the US; exclusivity still runs to ~2031–32.
Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149 a month cash through TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
Indiana and Arkansas Medicaid 1115 waivers still make GLP-1 coverage conditional on ≥80% refill adherence and quarterly verified weigh-ins, with a 12-month lockout after two missed checks.

prose.headline: One in four of us is on it. A pill made it cheap, the label says it can flatten you, and Saturday is now the day off.
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2030 about one American adult in four is taking an incretin drug, roughly 64 million people, up from 26 million two years earlier. The country did not decide this. A pill made it possible. In August 2029 the FDA approved Novo Nordisk's oral amycretin, which matched tirzepatide's weight loss in a head-to-head trial. TrumpRx priced it at $149 a month to start and $249 at maintenance. The older pills, Foundayo and the Wegovy pill, still start at $149. For most of the middle class, the drug now costs about as much as a phone bill, and there is no needle.

The expansion happened mostly in cash. Employers drew the opposite conclusion from the same volume curve. Only 43 percent of large employers still cover the drugs for weight loss. Many replaced coverage with employee-paid direct contracts that cost almost exactly what TrumpRx charges anyone. Plans now pay for diabetes, heart, sleep-apnea and kidney codes, and their auditors read those codes closely. Nearly half of all users pay out of pocket. Another five million buy Indian pens and pills by mail, which the FDA seizes now and then but has never prosecuted.

The bottom third got in another way. When semaglutide was approved for smoking cessation in March 2029, a decade-old federal rule required Medicaid to cover it, in twelve-week courses. In Gary and in the Arkansas Delta, the way onto a weight drug now runs through a quitline, and the course ends on schedule whether or not the weight has come off. Indiana and Arkansas still run their adherence waivers, so the pharmacy-kiosk scale is still there.

Prices drift down without falling. Medicare renewed its Bridge programme at $199 a month with a $50 copay, and branded injectables on TrumpRx now cost $199 to $275. Wegovy's list price is still $1,349, and there is still no US generic.

The biggest change in daily life comes from a December 2029 label. The FDA wrote anhedonia into the warnings section of every incretin label, with a number: about six percent of users at maintenance doses lose a clinically meaningful amount of pleasure, against three percent on placebo, and about nine percent at the highest doses. Applied to 64 million users, that excess is roughly two million people. What had been the 'Ozempic personality' of think pieces became a clinical term. The new pills have short half-lives, so the remedy is easy: skip Friday and Saturday, then resume Sunday night. About a third of pill users say they skip on purpose at least once a month. Restaurants sell off-dose tasting menus. Managers notice that Tuesdays are quiet. The FDA added a line telling people not to restart at full dose, after emergency rooms reported Sunday-night vomiting.

The same mechanism is now sold as a cure. In September the FDA approved semaglutide for gambling disorder, its first indication for compulsion. Telehealth firms took this as permission to treat compulsive shopping and binge-streaming as well. Two weeks earlier, a rally in Nashville under the banner 'Unblunted' brought together fat-liberation organisers, natural-health influencers and Southern Baptist pastors. They agree on almost nothing except that appetite is not a disease. Their potlucks are deliberately abundant. In the same suburbs, family tables are split between people who eat and people who graze.

Snack and beer volumes fell again, this time in middle-income households. Gyms that pair a bone scan with coaching keep growing, though mostly among people who could already afford coaching. The bone warnings from 2027 still stand. Cash pill users mostly skip the scans, and nobody has studied a body that is medicated five days a week and free on the other two.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Reyes takes her pill at 5:40, before the coffee, standing at the sink. It's Thursday, so she takes it. Tomorrow she won't.

At the dental office in Tucson she cleans six mouths before lunch. A patient asks whether she's on it, then whether the pills are as good as the shots. 'Same,' Marisol says. 'Cheaper.' The patient says her husband's company stopped covering hers in January. Marisol's did too. Now $249 comes out of her checking account on the eighth, after the car payment.

Lunch is half a turkey wrap. She throws away the other half, and she isn't hungry.

At three, her sister Bea texts a photo of the Saturday potluck menu from her church: green-chile stew, tres leches, tamales. *Unblunted,* the flyer says in gold script. *Come hungry.* Marisol types *maybe* and deletes it, then types *I'll bring the rice.*

Her daughter Ines, fourteen, is at the kitchen table when Marisol gets home, eating cereal straight from the box. Ines watches her mother pour half a glass of wine, sip it, and leave it.

'Are you blunted or just tired?' Ines asks, in the voice of the commercial.

'Tired.'

After Ines goes to bed, Marisol reads the folded Medication Guide she keeps in the junk drawer. *Anhedonia. About 6 in 100.* Under it: *Do not restart at your full dose if you miss more than 3 days.*

She sets an alarm for Sunday, 9 p.m., and labels it *back on*. She takes the tres leches out of the freezer to thaw for Saturday.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Of the 16.5 pts who had used by 2028, 11.2 are on now (about 6.4 who stayed on plus 4.8 off-now people who restarted, mostly on pills) and 5.3 are off.
least_plausible_claims.why: This implies about 65% of 2028 current users stayed on for two years and about 73% of the off-now group restarted. That conflicts with the ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart-within-a-year figures the parent world sets. The cycling arithmetic reconciles only because these retention rates are asserted. Fails mechanism and magnitude.

least_plausible_claims.quote: gambling disorder, adjunct to CBT in adults (semaglutide, Sep 2030): the first 'compulsion' indication
least_plausible_claims.why: The parent world had gambling use as 'still anecdotal', and no filing event is stated. A phase 3 started in 2027 would not plausibly read out, be filed, and be approved by Sep 2030 under a 12-month-after-filing rule. The 'priority review' wording does not close the gap. Fails magnitude on approval timing.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Most of the growth from 2.6M comes through the smoking-cessation indication (Mar 2029).
least_plausible_claims.why: It asserts that about 2.6M additional Medicaid users are on 12-week courses at any one time within 21 months. States can still use prior authorisation and step therapy, and semaglutide is only an adjunct to standard therapy. The mandate-to-uptake chain is asserted, not shown. Fails mechanism.

rationale.badness: About 2M people carry drug-attributable anhedonia. A roughly 35M-person unmonitored cash and import tier skips DEXA while bone harm from cycling is confirmed. Built-in on/off cycling comes from 12-week Medicaid courses and employer withdrawals (open_tensions). Employer coverage is withdrawn, and the Indiana and Arkansas waivers persist. The body_and_culture severity of 5 and a politicised appetite register as real cohesion losses. Offsets: cheaper access and a harm that is now labelled, quantified and discussed, which keeps the epistemic score low. This is a harder society with new losers, not a structurally hidden harm.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Every driver is visible in fields and events: 24.2% adoption, managed-decline pricing in Jan 2030, employer coverage 43%, the gambling indication, the Dec 2029 anhedonia label, oral amycretin, the Unblunted backlash, and mainstream-complaint framing. No market shock or new state action appears, and the Bridge renewal is a continuation. mechanism: Payer shifts and the cessation pathway are mostly shown, but the persistence and restart rates (claim 1) and the Medicaid cessation uptake (claim 3) are asserted. Attributing most of the surge to one oral launch is also weak, because $149 pills already existed in 2028. magnitude: Current use (24.2%) is inside the envelope and ever-use (33.6%) is near its top. Payer shares sum to 100%, the age bands and income thirds sum correctly, and the Bridge ($8.6B) and cash ($66B) arithmetic holds. The gambling approval timing (claim 2) is doubtful against the 12-month rule.
rationale.generativity: The Marisol vignette shows rather than explains: the Thursday pill, the Sunday 9 p.m. 'back on' alarm, Ines's 'blunted or tired' line and the tres leches. The world adds recognisable roles and settings, such as the dental hygienist, Gary and the Arkansas Delta, Friday 'off-day' plates, off-dose tasting menus and Nashville rallies. The prose supplies several ready scenes and characters.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Semaglutide gained smoking cessation (Mar 2029) and gambling disorder (Sep 2030, priority review, built on a phase 3 that an NIH–academic consortium started in 2027).
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism and approval timing. The 2028 parent calls gambling use 'still anecdotal' and mentions no trial. The candidate adds a 2027 phase 3 after the fact and shows no filing event, yet reaches approval by Sep 2030, which strains the 12-months-after-filing rule.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide postmarketing studies used SHAPS (Snaith-Hamilton Pleasure Scale) and found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~9% at top doses against ~3% on placebo.
least_plausible_claims.why: Fails mechanism. Retatrutide was approved in Mar 2028 with allocated supply, and FDA only requested an anhedonia scale in the parent. A powered postmarketing readout, a pooled reanalysis and a class-wide Warnings label by Dec 2029 is implausibly fast, with no chain shown.

About 45M new starters would have to arrive in roughly 16 months, though $149 orals (Foundayo, Wegovy pill) already existed in 2028 without driving adoption.
